chunks: And Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying:

“Regarding the mukātab, there was a period when people did not stipulate that if he became unable, then he would be returned to slavery. But today they do stipulate this, and the Muslims are bound by their conditions. And he is flogged in the hadd punishment according to the measure of what has been freed of him.”
I said: “What do you think—if half of him has been freed, is his testimony in divorce admissible?”
He said: “If there is with him a man and a woman, his testimony is admissible.”

key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبِ: a slave under a contractual agreement of emancipation
key_terms.شُرُوطِهِمْ: their stipulated conditions in a binding agreement

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a mukātab who fails his contract, and is the testimony of a partially freed slave accepted in divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning the mukātab, including contractual stipulations about return to slavery upon inability to fulfill the contract and the proportional application of hadd punishment according to the degree of emancipation. It also addresses the admissibility of testimony in divorce for a partially emancipated mukātab when joined by other qualifying witnesses.
